title: USAir 1493
summary: USAir Flight 1493, a Boeing 737, collided with SkyWest Airlines Flight 5569, a Fairchild Metroliner, on runway 24L at Los Angeles International Airport. The local controller was distracted by a misplaced flight progress strip and an aircraft that inadvertently switched off the tower frequency. Confused about the position of the SkyWest aircraft, the controller cleared both aircraft to use the same runway. The USAir 737 crushed the Metroliner, resulting in 35 fatalities.
probable_cause: Inadequate procedures at LAX control tower that provided insufficient redundancy, leading to loss of situational awareness by the local controller, and inadequate FAA oversight of control tower management.

title: Ryan International Airlines 590
summary: A McDonnell Douglas DC-9-15RC cargo flight crashed on takeoff from Cleveland Hopkins International Airport during icing conditions. The flight crew failing to deice their aircraft contributed to the accident. The captain had 10,505 flight hours including 505 hours on the DC-9, while the first officer had 3,820 flight hours including 510 hours on the DC-9. Both pilots were killed when the aircraft rolled 90 degrees to the left and entered a stall shortly after liftoff.
probable_cause: The causes of the crash were the flight crew failing to deice their aircraft, and the inexperience of the Federal Aviation Administration, McDonnell Douglas, and Ryan International Airlines with icing condition on DC-9-10 aircraft.

Both engines began to experience compressor stalls and the stick shaker activated. The aircraft rolled 90 degrees to the left and entered a stall.
The aircraft rolled 90 degrees to the left and entered a stall, then crashed back onto runway 23L.

title: LAN Chile 1069
summary: LAN Chile Flight 1069 was cleared for a VOR A approach to Puerto Williams on runway 26, but the captain decided to perform a direct approach to runway 08. The aircraft touched down 427 meters from the runway threshold at 112 knots on a wet runway with a negative slope and little braking action. The aircraft was unable to stop and overran the runway into the Beagle Channel. The investigation determined the probable cause was poor planning in changing runways and misapplication of the landing procedure.
probable_cause: The probable cause was a failure of good planning made by the pilot during the approach when he decided to change runway and misapplication of the landing procedure. The weather conditions, negative slope, wet runway, wind and little braking action led to the overrun of the runway.

title: United Airlines 585
summary: A Boeing 737-291 experienced a sudden rudder hardover on final approach to Colorado Springs. Prior to the fatal accident, the rudder abruptly deflected on February 25 and again on February 27, but these incidents were not fully resolved. On March 3, the aircraft rolled over and entered an uncontrolled dive on final approach, killing all 25 aboard. The NTSB eventually determined the crash resulted from a design defect in the 737's rudder power control unit.

title: Aeropostal Alas de Venezuela 108
summary: Flight 109 took off from La Chinita International Airport with 45 passengers and crew. Several minutes later the McDonnell Douglas DC-9-32 crashed on the side of a foggy mountain near The Guillotine in the Páramo Los Torres and burst into flames. Because of fog in the area, the pilots did not know they were on a collision course with the mountain.

title: An-24 crash in Navoiy
summary: Flight from Tashkent to Navoiy with 4 crew and 59 passengers. During approach, crew provided false altitude information to controller, reporting 2,100 meters when actually at 3,000 meters, then 1,500 meters when at 2,400 meters. Pilot initiated steep descent at 20 m/s with airspeed reaching 450 km/h. Aircraft passed over runway threshold at 30 meters altitude at excessive speed of 350 km/h and landed long 710 meters past threshold. Unable to stop, aircraft overran at 225 km/h, lost undercarriage, and collided with concrete blocks. All four crew and 30 passengers died.
probable_cause: Crew provided false position and altitude reports to ATC, resulting in descent below safe altitude and an unstabilized approach at excessive speed that could not be arrested within remaining runway.

title: Singapore Airlines 117
summary: Singapore Airlines Flight 117 was hijacked en route from Kuala Lumpur to Singapore on 26 March 1991 by four Pakistani terrorists armed with explosives and knives. The aircraft landed safely at Changi Airport. During negotiations, two flight attendants were pushed out of the aircraft. title: 1991 Merion mid-air collision
summary: A Piper Aerostar with a nose gear indication problem received a low pass from a Bell 412 helicopter to visually inspect the gear status. The helicopter crew attempted to determine if the nose gear was locked but the task was futile due to the gear door design that obscured the locking mechanism. The two aircraft collided during the inspection maneuver, both catching fire and crashing onto Merion Elementary School grounds. All five occupants of both aircraft were killed; two children on the ground were also killed.

title: Atlantic Southeast Airlines 2311
summary: Atlantic Southeast Airlines Flight 2311, an Embraer EMB 120 Brasilia with 23 aboard, crashed north of Brunswick, Georgia on April 5, 1991 during approach to landing. The NTSB investigation determined that the left propeller control unit malfunctioned, allowing the left propeller to overspeed with its blades oriented nearly perpendicular to the direction of flight. This created severe asymmetric thrust with insufficient thrust on the left side, causing a left roll that exceeded pilot recovery capability. The crew did not perceive the problem until the propeller blade angle reached 22-26 degrees, at which point the aircraft became very difficult to control.
probable_cause: A malfunction of the left propeller control unit allowed the left propeller to overspeed, creating severe asymmetric thrust that rolled the aircraft to the left beyond the pilot's control authority to recover.

factors.evidence: Propeller control unit malfunction allowed left propeller to overspeed with blades nearly perpendicular to direction of flight, creating asymmetric thrust condition.

title: Air Tahiti 805
summary: Air Tahiti Flight 805, a Dornier 228-212, crashed into the water behind Nuku Hiva Airport while on approach, killing 10 of 22 occupants. The crew indicated an intent to land on runway 24 despite air traffic control instructions to use runway 06. At 700 feet altitude and 400 meters from runway 24, both propellers failed. The aircraft made left and right turns before crashing into the water. Investigation found the pilots' inappropriate response to the engine failure as the primary cause.

title: Aeroflot 8556
summary: Aeroflot Flight 8556 crashed 13 meters short of the runway on approach to Pulkovo Airport. The aircraft began descent from 10,100 meters as weather deteriorated with heavy rain and a cumulonimbus cloud. During descent at 200 meters, the rate of descent increased to 7.5 meters per second and the aircraft slipped below the glideslope. The approach continued and rate of descent reached 7 meters per second again. At 20 meters altitude, the crew realized the danger and tried to stop descent, but the aircraft struck the ground short of the runway.
probable_cause: The approach was destabilized due to multiple factors. The actions of the crew were inconsistent and uncoordinated. There was no assistance from the approach controller in the final stages of the flight. The accident could have been avoided had the pilots initiated a go-around once they realized the approach was unstable.

factors.evidence: Heavy rain and a cumulonimbus cloud were present and not transmitted to the crew.

The controllers were replaced during the approach in violation of procedure, and there was no assistance from the approach controller in the final stages of flight.
The approach continued and the accident could have been avoided had the pilots initiated a go-around once they realized the approach was unstable.
The aircraft struck the ground 13 meters short of the runway, the landing gear collapsed and the fuselage broke into three pieces.

title: Lauda Air 004
summary: Lauda Air Flight 004, a Boeing 767-300ER flying from Hong Kong via Bangkok to Vienna, crashed into mountainous jungle terrain in Thailand on 26 May 1991 after the thrust reverser on the No. 1 engine deployed uncommanded during the climb. The pilots had received an EICAS advisory about a possible reverser fault nine minutes earlier but took no remedial action, believing it a false indication. The reverser deployment disrupted airflow over the wing, causing a 25% loss of lift and an aerodynamic stall; the aircraft entered a diving left turn and in-flight breakup, killing all 223 people on board.
probable_cause: Thailand's Aircraft Accident Investigation Committee determined the probable cause to be an uncommanded in-flight deployment of the left engine thrust reverser, which resulted in loss of flight path control; the specific cause of the deployment was not positively identified.

factors.evidence: The No. 1 engine reverser deployed while the plane was over mountainous jungle terrain, and Thurner's last recorded words were 'Oh, reverser's deployed.'
After consulting the aircraft's Quick Reference Handbook, they determined that the alert was 'coming on and off' and that it was 'just an advisory thing.'
The accident report states that the 'flight crew training simulators yielded erroneous results' and that recovery from the loss of lift 'was uncontrollable for an unexpecting flight crew.'
An aerodynamic plume of air disrupted the airflow over the leading edge of the left wing during the engine's rundown to idle thrust, which resulted in a 25% loss of lift and an aerodynamic stall.
The aircraft immediately began a diving left turn, resulting in an uncontrolled dive and in-flight breakup.

events.text: At 23:08, Welch and Thurner received a visual warning indication on the EICAS display that a possible system failure would cause the thrust reverser on the No. 1 engine to deploy in flight.

At 23:17, the No. 1 engine reverser deployed while the plane was over mountainous jungle terrain, and Thurner's last recorded words were 'Oh, reverser's deployed.'
An aerodynamic plume of air disrupted the airflow over the leading edge of the left wing, causing a 25% loss of lift and an aerodynamic stall, and the aircraft immediately began a diving left turn.
The aircraft suffered an uncontrolled dive and in-flight breakup, killing all 213 passengers and ten crew members on board.

title: Nigeria Airways 2120
summary: Nigeria Airways Flight 2120 caught fire shortly after takeoff from Jeddah on July 11, 1991, when underinflated tires overheated and burst on the runway. The crew was unaware of the fire in the wheel assembly area and attempted to return for an emergency landing, but lost flight control capability as the fire consumed hydraulic and electrical systems. summary: Continental Express Flight 2574, an Embraer EMB 120 Brasilia, crashed near Eagle Lake, Texas during descent while initiating landing sequence. title: 1991 RAAF Boeing 707 crash
summary: A Boeing 707 conducting conversion training in a non-approved demonstration of asymmetric flight stalled and entered a spin. The instructor had disabled the rudder hydraulic boost and reduced speed to minimum controllable airspeed (VMCA) with two left engines at idle, creating a condition requiring extreme rudder force. The aircraft stalled, and despite crew attempting to re-engage hydraulic boost, there was insufficient altitude to recover before impact into Bass Strait.
probable_cause: The instructor devised a demonstration of asymmetric flight that was inherently dangerous and certain to lead to a sudden departure from controlled flight. Contributing factors included the instructor's significant experience in the P-3 Orion where similar exercises were successful, leading to underestimation of the hazard. Broader organisational issues included loss of operational knowledge as pilots left the air force and inadequacies in 707 documentation and training.

Instructor Lewin briefed asymmetric thrust exercise with both left engines at idle and no hydraulic rudder assistance
First Officer Ellis turned off rudder boost, configured aircraft with flaps 25, began reducing speed toward VMCA
Ellis banked aircraft to maintain heading while in sideslip, increased power on right engines as aircraft slowed to 148 knots
Lewin told Ellis to 'wrestle with the beastie' as Ellis struggled with physical workload to maintain control
Pilots discussed how to get out of situation as stick shaker sounded, indicating stall
Aircraft stalled, entered spin, descended close to vertically completing two full revolutions, crew attempted to re-engage hydraulic rudder boost but insufficient altitude remained to recover

title: Aeroflot-Yugavia 519
summary: The Yakovlev Yak-40 crashed into Mt. Kukurtbash 23 kilometres from Makhachkala Airport after the crew descended below safe altitude off the established approach pattern. title: 1991 Azerbaijani Mil Mi-8 shootdown
summary: The Mil Mi-8 helicopter carrying a peacekeeping observation team of Azerbaijani government officials and Russian and Kazakhstani officials was shot down en route from Aghdam to Martuni on November 20, 1991 amidst heavy fighting. The helicopter was struck by ZSU-23-4 Shilka anti-aircraft fire and SA-6 missiles near the village of Berdashen, killing all 22 people aboard including peacekeeping officials, journalists and crew. The attack disrupted ongoing peace talks during the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.
probable_cause: The helicopter was shot down by large-caliber ground-based anti-aircraft weapons (ZSU-23-4 Shilka and SA-6 missiles) fired from the ground during armed conflict in an area where rising tension and escalation had been noted.

factors.evidence: team of observers along with representatives of Azerbaijani government were to fly from Aghdam to Martuni due to rising tension in the district
peacekeeping mission coordination between sides failed despite Zheleznovodsk communique; Armenian side had ceased peace talks
helicopter was shot down en route with a group of ZSU-23-4 Shilka and SA-6 missiles, killing everyone on board
investigation was initiated but was suspended and no one was indicted because the area of the crash was soon captured by Armenian militants

events.text: On the eve of the crash, the Armenian side ceased the peace talks with Azerbaijan; the team of observers along with representatives of Azerbaijani government were to fly from Aghdam to Martuni due to rising tension in the district

All 22 people on board were killed in the crash; the attack on the helicopter disrupted the ongoing peace talks

title: Scandinavian Airlines System 751
summary: Scandinavian Airlines Flight 751, an MD-81 departing Stockholm Arlanda Airport, encountered dual engine failure 76 and 78 seconds after takeoff at an altitude of 3,220 feet after clear ice accumulated on the wings' inner roots and broke off, being ingested into both engines. The ice deformed fan blades, causing compressor stalls and engine surges that led to both engine failures. The pilots executed a successful emergency landing in a field near Gottröra with no fatalities among the 129 occupants.
probable_cause: Clear ice had formed on the upper side of the wings before takeoff but was not detected. De-icing fluid was applied but the aircraft was not checked afterwards for remaining ice as required. Ice pieces broke off during takeoff and were ingested into both engines, causing compressor stalls, engine surges, and complete engine failure. Contributing factors included inadequate training on engine surge recovery and insufficient information to the crew about the automatic thrust restoration system.

factors.evidence: Clear ice had formed on the upper side of the wings before takeoff but was not detected; approximately 2550 kg of very cold, flight-chilled fuel remained in the wing tanks
The aircraft was de-iced with 850 L of de-icing fluid, but not checked afterwards for remaining ice by the de-icing personnel or the Pilot-in-Charge, which he was required to do
There was no simulator or other training on the engine surging problem; they were not trained in restoring engine operation after repeated surges

An automatic system, ATR (automatic thrust restoration), had not been described to the flight crew by SAS; SAS took part in theme conferences addressing clear ice but ATR was not documented within SAS
Engine no. 1 surged 39 seconds after takeoff and both engines failed at 76 and 78 seconds respectively, leaving the aircraft with no thrust
With the aircraft emerging from cloud cover at 890 feet altitude, the pilots successfully executed an emergency landing in a field near Gottröra with all 129 occupants surviving

events.text: Aircraft arrived at Stockholm Arlanda Airport and was parked overnight; clear ice formed on upper side of wings due to approximately 2550 kg of very cold flight-chilled fuel remaining in wing tanks
Aircraft was de-iced with 850 liters of de-icing fluid but not checked afterwards for remaining ice by de-icing personnel or Pilot-in-Charge
Plane departed Stockholm; pieces of ice broke off and were ingested into fans of both engines
Noises and vibrations caused by no. 2 engine surging first noticed; flight crew throttled down but automatic thrust restoration simultaneously increased throttle, causing surges to continue
Both engines failed at 76 and 78 seconds after takeoff at altitude of 3,220 feet; pilots executed emergency landing in field near Gottröra with no fatalities

title: China Airlines 358
summary: China Airlines Flight 358, a Boeing 747-200F freighter, reported problems with number 3 engine several minutes after takeoff from Taipei at 5000 feet. The crew requested a left turn to return to the airport but reported being unable to turn left moments later. The aircraft struck a hill near Wanli at 700 feet. Investigation revealed the number 3 engine and pylon had separated from the aircraft due to failure of pylon midspar fittings.
probable_cause: Failure of pylon midspar fittings attaching engine pylon to wing, resulting in separation of number 3 engine and pylon, loss of control, and impact with terrain.

factors.evidence: The pylon midspar fittings, which attach the pylon to the lower portion of the wing front spar, had failed.
The number 3 engine and its pylon had separated from the aircraft and struck the number 4 engine.
Crew reported they were unable to turn left and this was the last radio contact made by the crew.
The aircraft struck a hill, right wing first, near Wanli at 700 ft altitude.

events.text: Several minutes after takeoff at 5000 feet, crew reports problems with number 3 engine.
ATC vectors aircraft for left turn to return; approximately 2 minutes later crew reports unable to turn left.
Aircraft struck hill near Wanli, right wing first, at 700 feet altitude; crew lost control of aircraft.

notes: Pylon failure investigations led to Boeing-wide modifications
Similar incident (El Al 1862) occurred 10 months later with nearly identical cause
